name: Bug report
description: Report something in Mahalath that isn't working as expected.
labels: ["bug"]
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: |
        Thanks for filing a bug. A small, self-contained reproduction plus the
        details below is the fastest path to a fix.

        **Please don't paste secrets.** Scrub any MongoDB connection string
        (`mongodb://user:pass@…`) or Anthropic API key from logs and config
        before posting.
  - type: textarea
    id: what-happened
    attributes:
      label: What happened?
      description: What did you do, what did you expect, and what happened instead?
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: repro
    attributes:
      label: Steps to reproduce
      description: Minimal CLI commands or steps (e.g. the input document and config) that trigger the bug.
      render: shell
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: dropdown
    id: install
    attributes:
      label: Installed via
      options:
        - Python source / editable install
        - Other (describe above)
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: input
    id: version
    attributes:
      label: Mahalath version / commit
      description: Release tag, or `git rev-parse --short HEAD` for a source checkout.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: input
    id: mongo
    attributes:
      label: MongoDB version
      description: e.g. "MongoDB 8.0".
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: input
    id: model
    attributes:
      label: Model adapter / model
      description: e.g. "local Ollama gemma3:1b" or "Claude API review enabled".
    validations:
      required: false
  - type: input
    id: env
    attributes:
      label: Python & OS
      description: e.g. "Python 3.11 on Ubuntu 22.04 (WSL2)".
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: logs
    attributes:
      label: Relevant logs / traceback
      description: Any error output. Scrub credentials first.
      render: shell
    validations:
      required: false

name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*.*.*"

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
          cache: "pip"
      - name: Build sdist and wheel
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip build
          python -m build --sdist --wheel --outdir dist
          shopt -s nullglob
          wheels=(dist/*-py3-none-any.whl)
          sdists=(dist/*.tar.gz)
          if [[ ${#wheels[@]} -ne 1 || ${#sdists[@]} -ne 1 ]]; then
            echo "expected exactly one wheel and one sdist" >&2
            ls -l dist || true
            exit 1
          fi
          python -m venv /tmp/rel
          /tmp/rel/bin/pip install --upgrade pip
          /tmp/rel/bin/pip install "${wheels[0]}"
          /tmp/rel/bin/python -c "import mahalath; print(mahalath.__version__)"
      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          generate_release_notes: true
          files: |
            dist/*.whl
            dist/*.tar.gz
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
        # Requires a Trusted Publisher on PyPI for this repo + release.yml

name: Tests

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - "**"
  pull_request:

jobs:
  pytest:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      mongo:
        image: mongo:8.0
        ports:
          - 27017:27017
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "mongosh --quiet --eval 'db.runCommand({ ping: 1 }).ok'"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 12

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install package
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          python -m pip install -e ".[dev,web,hoglah]" "galeed @ git+https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/galeed" ruff

      - name: Lint (ruff)
        run: |
          ruff check src tests

      - name: Run tests
        run: |
          python -m pytest

# Changelog

All notable changes to Mahalath are documented here.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed
- Semantic grounding now requires a final critic ratification of the
  explorer's exact wording, rejects short and wrapped verbatim external
  copies, preserves failed grounding calls in the audit trail, attributes
  stored prose to its actual author model, and includes the grounding round
  in persisted transcript iteration counts.

### Added
- **Semantic grounding (ADR-038).** After the ordinary corpus debate,
  Mahalath can consult external passages without making them a second
  ontology. `semantic_grounding.mode` is `corpus_only` (the default; no
  lookup), `hybrid` (lookup only when the corpus minimum confidence is
  strictly below `external_lookup_threshold`), or `external` (always
  look up after the corpus debate). A revision is stored only when both
  agents call it faithful to the source, neither challenges or dismisses
  the passages, the wording is not copied from an external passage, and
  the pair is at least as confident as the corpus debate. A challenge
  keeps the corpus wording and cannot raise confidence. Retrieval or
  model failure leaves the corpus decision. The attempt is audited on
  the same `decision_log_id` and in `semantic_grounding`. Sources are a
  local JSON file, MediaWiki search snippets, or an operator HTTP
  endpoint. `MAHALATH_GROUNDING_MODE` and `MAHALATH_GROUNDING_THRESHOLD`
  override the YAML.
- **Overnight grounding toggle.** `semantic_grounding.overnight`
  (default off; `MAHALATH_GROUNDING_OVERNIGHT`) lets the stale-entry
  redefine pass — the scheduler's REM job and `redefine-stale` — run
  semantic grounding after its source-first rewrite. Off, that pass
  does not retrieve, even when `mode` is `hybrid` or `external`. On,
  lookup follows `mode` and `external_lookup_threshold`. A rewrite
  still below the redefine confidence floor is not appended; an
  invoked lookup is still audited. REM re-debate of undecided items,
  ingest, and manual redebate keep following `mode` on their own.

## [1.6.0] — 2026-08-11

First operation of ADR-036 against the live corpus, and what it exposed.

### Added
- **`runtime.relatedness_model`** — the model that judges document relatedness,
  separate from the debate default (`None` → `runtime.model`), matching the
  existing per-role override pattern. Threaded through both call sites: the
  `link-documents` CLI (explicit `--model` still wins) and the ingest hook —
  without the second, turning the knob would have fixed the manual command and
  left automatic linking on the fast model.

  Pinning it matters. Judging "same work vs merely the same topic" requires
  reading both documents rather than reasoning from their titles, and a small
  model does not. Measured on the live corpus: `gemma2:2b` called an English
  ontology and an unrelated German pilot a `translation` at confidence 8.0,
  inferring it from the word "Edition"; `mistral-small` returned not-related at
  9.5 on the identical prompt. Both were confident, so raising
  `--min-confidence` is no substitute for a capable judge.
- `link_related_documents` and `relatedness_model` documented in
  `config.example.yaml` (neither was discoverable before).

### Fixed
- **Relatedness refuses to judge a document whose text cannot be read.**
  `_sample()` returned an empty string when the archived file was missing, and
  the judge was then handed a *title* to compare against a full document —
  producing a confident verdict from no evidence and recording it as a link.
  Found on the live corpus, where one document's archive had been deleted while
  its database record remained. Now raises for the incoming document and skips
  unreadable candidates without spending a model call.

### Notes
- Requires **hoglah >= 0.10.0** on the *worker daemon*, not just the client. A
  0.9.0 daemon cannot deserialise a request carrying `depends_on`,
  `idempotency_key`, `retry_policy` or `run_at` and fails every job with
  Hoglah's generic `"Unexpected worker error"`. Symptom: jobs enqueue, run and
  fail with no usable reason. Fix: upgrade and restart the daemon.

## [1.5.0] — 2026-08-11

### Added
- **Conversation history for every prose layer (ADR-034).** Every model call
  that contributes prose to a term now writes a `decision_log` row plus its
  `agent_exchanges`, linked from the definition and readable. `detailed_text`
  previously recorded *nothing* — the prompt and response were lost the moment
  the call returned — and now carries `detailed_model_used`,
  `detailed_created_at` and `detailed_decision_log_id` distinct from the
  debate's. New `mahalath show-decision <id|MPL-label>` (with `--verbose`,
  `--layer`, `--json`), a "How this term was arrived at" table on the entry
  page, and a `/decisions/{id}` view with collapsible prompts. Prose is not
  stored if its audit write fails: better no exposition than one with no record
  of where it came from. Expansions use the non-debate outcome `elaborated` and
  are excluded from debate statistics so acceptance rates stay about debates.
- **Operator review gated on confidence after recursion (ADR-037).**
  `/undecided` is now a review queue rather than a list of everything pending:
  terms surface once attempted `REVIEW_ESCALATION_THRESHOLD` (2) times and
  still below `runtime.confidence_threshold`, or immediately for `conflict` and
  `moderator_block`, which re-debate does not resolve. Undebated `proposed_term`
  entries never surface. The page reports how many items are still being
  retried, so an empty queue reads as "nothing needs you" rather than "nothing
  is happening". Accept/reject actions on the page and via
  `mahalath needs-review` / `accept-undecided` / `reject-undecided`, writing to
  a new `operator_decisions` audit collection. An operator accept mints its own
  `decision_log_id` and names the debate it overrode.
- **Related-document linking and term correspondence (ADR-036).** New
  `mahalath link-documents` asks the model whether an incoming document is
  related to one already processed (revision, translation, excerpt, shared
  material) and records the link; `--correspond` matches terms across the pair.
  `mahalath compare-documents <link-id>` reports shared terms, terms unique to
  each side, and definitions that differ — the first way to answer "did that
  model or process change improve the output?". **Not deduplication:** the
  incoming document is processed in full and the original's terms are never
  modified. Opt-in at ingest via `runtime.link_related_documents`.
- **Design (ADR-033):** scholarly layer + same-document lesson memory —
  [`docs/scholarly-layer.md`](docs/scholarly-layer.md). Three prose layers per
  sense; debate transcripts remain ground truth. The lesson-memory half is
  **deferred to DQ-015**; the transcript half shipped as ADR-034.

### Fixed
- **Redefine-generated expositions had no corpus text (ADR-035).** The accept
  path passed a source snippet; the redefine path did not, so a definition
  rewritten overnight was asked to describe corpus usage with none in front of
  it and the model invented an example. New `source_snippet_for_entry` supplies
  a passage, preferring the triggering document.
- **The triggering document is recorded, not `source_document_ids[0]`.** 33 of
  119 live entries carry several sources, so the first one is a guess;
  `redefine_stale_entry` and `redebate_entry` now accept
  `triggering_document_id`, and the multi-source fallback is logged. This is
  the ADR-033 prerequisite: without it, same-document scoping would filter
  correctly over the wrong material.
- **`backfill-detailed --max-items` bounds attempts, not successes.** With a
  failing model it previously walked the entire collection regardless of the
  limit (3 requested → 20 attempted in a 20-entry probe). Now matches the
  `backfill-intents` / `backfill-contexts` pattern. Failures also report the
  adapter's own message instead of a fixed `"generation failed"`.

# Contributing to Mahalath

Thanks for your interest in Mahalath. This guide covers local development.

## Development setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/mahalath
cd mahalath
python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

Configuration lives in `config.yaml` (local, gitignored), with
`config.example.yaml` as the committed template. The runtime folders `input/`,
`processed/`, `ontology/`, `logs/`, and `undecided/` are gitignored (the folders
are committed via `.gitkeep`, their contents are not).

## Running tests

Integration tests need a MongoDB server on `localhost:27017` (for example
`docker run -d -p 27017:27017 mongo:8.0`).

```bash
pytest
```

## Code conventions

- Python 3.11+
- Source under `src/mahalath/`, tests under `tests/`
- Decisions are recorded (append-only) in `docs/architecture-decisions.md`

## Standing principles

These follow from `docs/requirements-v0.1.md` and apply by default:

- **Review-based writes.** Semantic/ontology writes stay review-based; no
  autonomous agent write authority before review queues, audit logs, and
  rollback exist.
- **Source-preserved.** Ingestion never silently rewrites, compresses, or
  summarises source documents — the source is authoritative; derived content is
  regeneratable.
- Please open an issue before changes that alter source preservation, agent
  write authority, the adapter boundary, or any "Out of scope" item in
  `docs/requirements-v0.1.md` §7.

## Reporting issues

Bugs and questions: <https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/mahalath/issues>. Security
issues: please report privately — see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

# Mahalath

**Mahalath turns a body of documents into a precise, auditable lexicon of
meanings, built by AI agents that debate each definition.** Drop Markdown
into `input/` and come back to a glossary with sharp definitions, a
parent/child hierarchy, several meanings per term where the corpus really
uses several, and full provenance. A retrieval API then lets another LLM
reason in those exact meanings rather than in ambiguous natural language.

It is local-first (MongoDB and Ollama). Frontier-model review through the
Anthropic API is optional.

## The idea

Natural language is ambiguous, and AI-to-AI reasoning suffers for it.
Mahalath gives every meaning an opaque, permanent label (`MPL-004`), one or
more debated definitions, a place in a hierarchy and a full audit trail.
Human words become approximate handles onto those meanings. One term can
hold several co-equal meanings, each tied to the *frame* it speaks within: a
`field` is one thing to a physicist, another to a farmer and another to a
database designer. A consuming LLM looks a term up, receives every codified
meaning with provenance, and cites the `(MPL label, frame)` pair it used.

A lexicon belongs to **one language**; the live one is English. Languages
are peers, never derived from each other. Cross-language relationships are
explicit, debated mapping assertions, never translation at ingestion.

## Is it for you?

**Good fit:** a corpus whose terms must be used precisely, such as a legal
code, an engineering handbook or a research literature, where you want
definitions that are argued, traceable and reviewable, and an ontology an
LLM can query.

**Not a fit:** a quick glossary of one document. Every term goes through
multi-agent debate on a local model, which takes time. It is also not a
translator: cross-language mappings relate meanings and do not translate
text.

## Try it

You need MongoDB running locally and Ollama with `gemma4:e2b` (debate)
pulled; `bge-m3` is only needed for cross-language mappings. Mahalath is
also on PyPI (`pip install "mahalath[web]"`).

```bash
# 1. Install
git clone https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/mahalath
cd mahalath
python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e ".[dev,web]"

# 2. Prerequisites: MongoDB running locally, and Ollama with the models
#    pulled (gemma4:e2b for debate; bge-m3 for cross-language mappings).
#      ollama pull gemma4:e2b
#      ollama pull bge-m3
.venv/bin/mahalath db-ping

# 3. Prepare a fresh database — creates every collection + index and
#    seeds the standard taxonomies. Idempotent; safe to re-run.
.venv/bin/mahalath init

# 4. Process a document
cp my-source.md input/
.venv/bin/mahalath process-input --max-terms 10

# 5. Browse the result
.venv/bin/mahalath list-ontology
.venv/bin/mahalath export-glossary --format md --out ontology/glossary.md

# 6. Query it like an LLM would
.venv/bin/mahalath retrieve "field" --format text --budget 800
.venv/bin/mahalath subtree MPL-001 --depth 2
.venv/bin/mahalath propose-term "lattice" --context "…source snippet…" --near MPL-004

# 7. See how a term was arrived at, and decide what the system couldn't
.venv/bin/mahalath show-decision MPL-001            # every conversation behind it
.venv/bin/mahalath show-decision MPL-001 --verbose  # including the prompts sent
.venv/bin/mahalath needs-review                     # only terms still stuck after retries
.venv/bin/mahalath accept-undecided <decision-log-id> --note "close enough"
```

## How it works

```
input/file.md  →  ingest + SHA-256 dedupe + archive
              →  heading-aware chunk (any document size)
              →  LLM-driven candidate term extraction
              →  multi-iteration debate (PrecisionCritic + SynthesisExplorer)
              →  optional external grounding (ADR-038), still on that debate:
                 corpus_only by default; hybrid or external when configured
              →  if accepted: ontology entry (frame-tagged definition; debate path
                 records a per-definition consensus score) + hierarchy review
                 pass (3-pass consensus)
              →  if undecided: queue for nightly REM re-debate
              →  reference extraction → reverse index → staleness cascade when
                 upstream entries change → audit/redefine self-healing
              →  glossary auto-export to ontology/glossary.{md,json}
```

Every model call is recorded with a `decision_log_id` and stays queryable;
every operator accept, reject or rollback writes to the same audit chain.
`mahalath show-decision MPL-001` replays the full conversation behind any
term.

## What you get

| Capability | In short |
|---|---|
| **Polysemy, first-class** | Definitions are tagged with a context frame; co-equal meanings never supersede each other |
| **Retrieval for LLMs** | Term search, full codified meanings, **token-budgeted bundles** that never drop a frame and always include every term a definition cites, subtree views and `propose-term`. Library, CLI and HTTP |
| **Review only what is stuck** | You are asked about a term only after the system has finished re-debating it (`needs-review`) |
| **Self-healing** | When an entry changes, every entry that cites it is flagged stale and re-audited overnight |
| **External grounding** | Optionally check a debated definition against outside sources; `corpus_only` by default |
| **Intent annotation** | *Why* the corpus uses a term (teach, warn, persuade…), admitted only when independent passes agree unanimously |
| **Self-analysis** | Calibration of agent confidence against your decisions, queue health and coverage (`mahalath effectiveness`) |
| **Style overlay** | Per-corpus voice notes that make definitions follow the source's framing; the biggest single quality lever in A/B testing |
| **Web UI and chat** | `mahalath serve`: browse, review and ask grounded questions with MPL citations |

Every capability, workflow and command in detail:
[docs/guide.md](docs/guide.md).

## Know before you rely on it

- **`frontier-review` sends content off your machine.** It sends the
  definitions under review and your style overlay to Anthropic's API (it
  needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). Everything else runs locally.
- **`consensus_score` is not comparable across paths.** Only the debate path
  records one. `null` or missing means "not a debate consensus", not zero.
- **External grounding is off by default**, and overnight rewrites stay
  inside the corpus unless `semantic_grounding.overnight` is enabled.
- **Design only, not built yet:** the scholarly layer and same-document
  lesson memory (ADR-033). Cross-language mappings work, but the live
  lexicon is English.

## Design commitments

- **Labels are immutable and opaque** — re-parenting moves tree edges, never the label; no semantics in the key (ADR-018/021).
- **Human labels are approximate interfaces, not the ontology** (ADR-019).
- **Languages are discrete peer lexicons** — a label addresses a meaning within one language's lexicon; cross-language equivalence is only ever an explicit, debated mapping assertion, and locale is metadata, never structure (ADR-028/029/030).
- **Retrieval surfaces all frames; the caller disambiguates** (ADR-022). **Returned meanings are reference-closed** (ADR-023).
- **Intent annotates definitions; it never creates entries or enters labels** (ADR-024).
- **Everything is auditable** — every accepted definition links to its debate transcript; every structural change is a proposal with a rollback path.

- **Self-analysis is read-only and file-snapshotted** — the effectiveness layer aggregates the audit trails it reports on but can never write to them (ADR-027).

The decision record (ADRs and open questions) is in
[docs/architecture-decisions.md](docs/architecture-decisions.md), and the
retrieval design is in [docs/retrieval-spec.md](docs/retrieval-spec.md).

## Status

Stage 2, deep. The self-sustaining loop works end to end: ingest, debate,
persist, hierarchy review, operator and frontier queues, nightly re-review,
self-healing and glossary export. So do the retrieval layer, the intent
extension and nightly self-analysis, all validated against a live corpus.
The test suite includes live MongoDB round-trips; the history is in
[CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

# Security Policy

Mahalath is an early local-first research prototype. Treat it as unsuitable for
untrusted network exposure until authentication, authorization, and data-handling
boundaries are explicitly designed and tested.

## Reporting a vulnerability

**Please do not open a public issue for security problems.**

Report privately via GitHub's
[private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/mahalath/security/advisories/new)
("Report a vulnerability" under the repository's **Security** tab). This keeps the
details private until a fix is available.

When reporting, please include the affected version/commit, a description, and
(ideally) a minimal reproduction.

## Handling credentials

Mahalath uses a MongoDB connection string and, optionally, an Anthropic Claude API
key for frontier-LLM review. Keep these in your local `config.yaml` (gitignored)
and scrub any connection strings or API keys from logs before sharing them in a
report.

mongo:
  uri: mongodb://localhost:27017
  # Distinct from Tirzah's database; same Mongo instance is fine.
  # See ADR-017.
  database: mahalath_dev

paths:
  # Operator drops new documents into input/. The ingestion worker
  # moves accepted files to processed/. See ADR-011, ADR-012.
  input: input
  processed: processed
  ontology: ontology
  logs: logs
  undecided: undecided

runtime:
  # Model adapter and model name. Initial runtime is Ollama; see ADR-005.
  # Default is ollama_http (no binary on PATH required). Use ollama_cli
  # only when you want to shell out to a local `ollama` executable.
  # llama-cpp-python remains an optional future path.
  model_adapter: ollama_http
  # After each accepted definition (debate / redefine), generate a longer
  # detailed_text exposition of the same sense (best-effort extra model call).
  # generate_detailed_definitions: true

  # ADR-036: on ingest, ask a model whether the incoming document is related to
  # one already processed (revision, translation, excerpt, shared material) and
  # record the link. NOT deduplication — the document is still processed in
  # full and the related document's terms are never touched; the link exists so
  # two runs over related material can be compared (`mahalath
  # compare-documents`). Costs one model call per already-processed document at
  # every ingest, so it is off by default and gets slower as the corpus grows.
  # link_related_documents: false
  #
  # The model that JUDGES relatedness. None -> `model` below. Worth pinning to
  # a larger family than the debate default: deciding "same work vs merely same
  # topic" requires reading both documents rather than reasoning from their
  # titles. Measured on a real corpus — gemma2:2b called an English ontology
  # and an unrelated German pilot a `translation` at confidence 8.0, inferring
  # it from the word "Edition"; mistral-small returned not-related at 9.5 on
  # the identical prompt. Both were confident, so raising --min-confidence is
  # no substitute for a capable judge.
  # relatedness_model: mistral-small:latest
  # gemma4:e2b chosen as Stage 1 default after a 2026-06-06 comparison
  # against gemma3:1b: 4.8x faster end-to-end (24s vs 1m58s on the
  # agonist-intro smoke), 1 iteration to acceptance vs 22-23, and
  # noticeably more domain-specific definitions. 7.2 GB on disk.
  model: gemma4:e2b

  # Multi-agent debate roles. Names per requirements §3.2 and DQ-001.
  # Moderator default off until first iteration cap is hit or first
  # contested split is detected. See DQ-001.
  # Each role may pin its own model (DQ-010): putting the debaters on
  # different model families makes min(pc, se) genuinely cross-model.
  # model: null -> the role uses runtime.model.
  agents:
    precision_critic:
      enabled: true
      system_prompt_path: null   # uses built-in default when null
      model: null                # e.g. mistral-small
    synthesis_explorer:
      enabled: true
      system_prompt_path: null
      model: null
    moderator:
      enabled: false
      system_prompt_path: null

  # Debate loop controls. Defaults per ADR-009 (iteration cap) and
  # ADR-010 (confidence threshold).
  # Consensus passes (hierarchy review + intent attribution) may
  # rotate across a model roster: pass i runs on consensus_models[i %
  # len]. Unanimity across model FAMILIES is much stronger evidence
  # than one model agreeing with itself N times. null -> every pass on
  # runtime.model.
  # consensus_models:
  #   - gemma4:e2b
  #   - mistral-small
  #   - qwen3.5:35b

  max_iterations_per_term: 50
  confidence_threshold: 8.0
  confidence_scale_max: 10.0

  # Resolved from PATH by default (portable). The HTTP path (ollama_base_url)
  # is preferred; only the `ollama_cli` adapter shells out to this binary.
  # Override for a non-PATH install, e.g. a WSL-mounted Windows binary:
  #   ollama_executable: /mnt/c/Users/<you>/AppData/Local/Programs/Ollama/ollama.exe
  # or set the OLLAMA_EXECUTABLE env var (Noa renders this from .env).
  ollama_executable: ollama
  # localhost for native installs. Under WSL2, embeddings need the
  # Windows host over HTTP — use the `wsl-gateway` sentinel host, which
  # auto-resolves to the WSL2 default gateway at startup (survives WSL
  # restarts) and requires OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0 on the Windows side:
  #   ollama_base_url: http://wsl-gateway:11434
  ollama_base_url: http://localhost:11434
  # Generous: the first call after idle loads the model from disk,
  # which takes minutes on laptop hardware.
  ollama_timeout_seconds: 600

  # Cross-language candidate shortlisting (M-C). The embedding model
  # turns a definition's meaning into a vector so candidate pairs are
  # found by meaning-closeness instead of a model eyeballing a list.
  # MUST be multilingual (bge-m3 covers 100+ languages incl. CJK).
  # Run `mahalath backfill-embeddings --apply` once it's pulled, then
  # `generate-mappings --candidate-source embedding`.
  embedding_model: bge-m3
  # embedding_adapter: null        # null -> use model_adapter
  mapping_candidate_source: auto   # auto | embedding | prompt
  mapping_candidate_top_k: 5

  # Route LLM calls (generation AND embeddings/fingerprinting) through a
  # Hoglah queue daemon instead of calling Ollama directly. Set
  # model_adapter / embedding_adapter / chat_adapter to "hoglah" to use it,
  # and install the extra:  pip install 'mahalath[hoglah]'.
  #
  # Topology: a SEPARATE `hoglah run` worker daemon executes jobs off the
  # shared SQLite queue (db_path) and writes results to output_dir. Mahalath
  # is a pure submitter — it enqueues, then either polls output_dir or gets an
  # HTTP callback. Point the daemon at the SAME db_path and output_dir, e.g.:
  #   HOGLAH_OUTPUT_DIR=~/.hoglah/outbox hoglah run --real
  hoglah:
    db_path: ~/.hoglah/hoglah.db
    output_dir: ~/.hoglah/outbox
    # How results come back: "poll" the output folder, or "callback" (Mahalath
    # runs a tiny HTTP receiver and Hoglah POSTs the result to it; falls back
    # to the output folder if a push is missed).
    delivery: callback
    poll_interval_seconds: 0.5
    # Callback receiver bind/advertise host + port (delivery: callback).
    # Both processes are local, so 127.0.0.1 works. port 0 = OS picks a free
    # port. Hoglah is given this URL per job; nothing is hardcoded on its side.
    callback_host: 127.0.0.1
    callback_port: 0

ingestion:
  # APScheduler-style polling cadence for the watched input folder.
  poll_interval_seconds: 60
  # SHA-256 duplicate rejection per ADR-016.
  duplicate_rejection: sha256

rem:
  # REM-style overnight processing cadence per requirements §3.4 and
  # DQ-009. Default fixed schedule.
  enabled: true
  cron: "0 2 * * *"     # 02:00 local time

# External semantic grounding (ADR-038). The source document stays
# primary. External passages may clarify, corroborate, challenge, or
# enrich a corpus-derived sense. They never silently replace it, and
# they are not a second ontology.
#
# mode:
#   corpus_only  default. No external lookup. Right for a corpus that
#                is treated as self-defining.
#   hybrid       look up only when the corpus debate's minimum
#                confidence is strictly below external_lookup_threshold.
#   external     always look up after the corpus debate.
#
# providers, in order: static (a local JSON file), wikipedia (MediaWiki
# search snippets only — result pages are not fetched), http (an
# operator endpoint returning {"hits": [...]}). An empty list records
# that nothing was configured and keeps the corpus decision.
semantic_grounding:
  mode: corpus_only
  external_lookup_threshold: 8.0
  # Stale-entry redefine (overnight REM job and `redefine-stale`)
  # consults external passages only when this is true. Off: `mode`
  # hybrid or external does not send that pass out to retrieve.
  # REM re-debate of undecided items follows `mode` either way.
  overnight: false
  providers: []
  max_hits: 5
  # min_relevance: 0.2          # cosine; omit to rank without dropping
  # static_path: grounding/passages.json
  # http_url: https://example.invalid/ground
  wikipedia_language: en
  timeout_seconds: 15
  # user_agent: null            # null -> Mahalath's default User-Agent

# Architecture Decisions

Last updated: 2026-09-30 (ADR-038)

An **Architecture Decision Record** (the `ADR-NNN` rows below) is one
design decision and the reasoning behind it. The `ADR` prefix is kept
only as a stable ID stamped on each decision and referenced elsewhere;
the term is spelled out here so the abbreviation never has to be known
cold. Records are append-only — if a decision is reversed, add a new one
rather than editing the old, and note the supersession in both entries.

## Accepted Decisions

| ID | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| ADR-001 | Use Python 3.11+ for core orchestration. | Best fit for local LLM tooling, MongoDB, and the multi-agent debate loop. Matches the operator's existing stack and matches Tirzah's choice. |
| ADR-002 | Use MongoDB as primary storage. | Flexible document shape suits the hybrid flat dictionary + hierarchical taxonomy required by §3.1. Same local instance Tirzah already uses; logical separation via a distinct database name. |
| ADR-003 | Avoid a dedicated graph database. | MongoDB adjacency-list patterns are sufficient for the ontology graph at the foreseeable scale (vocabulary, not corpus). Matches Tirzah ADR-003. |
| ADR-004 | All LLM calls behind an agent adapter. | Allows the local model stack to evolve (Gemma, Qwen, Mistral, future European variants) without rewriting the debate loop. Matches Tirzah ADR-004; lifted verbatim because it is load-bearing. |
| ADR-005 | Use Ollama as the initial local model runtime. | The operator already has Ollama configured for Tirzah. Avoid a second runtime install at bootstrap time. `llama-cpp-python` remains an optional future adapter. |
| ADR-006 | Hybrid flat + tree ontology layout. | Required by §3.1: flat dictionary for O(1) label lookup, hierarchical taxonomy for navigation and inheritance. Both views point at the same underlying entry records. |
| ADR-007 | Hierarchical numeric labels for ontology entries. | The operator-recommended `MPL-001.000.001a` format in §3.1 is the default. Format is enforceable per ADR-008. |
| ADR-008 | Label format and assignment is an agent decision, not a code constant. | §3.1 requires agents to decide label format. The format is recorded per ontology version and enforced by validation rather than hardcoded. |
| ADR-009 | Maximum 50 agent debate iterations per term before escalation. | Raised from §3.2's draft default of 25 after the 2026-06-06 Stage 1.7 live smoke showed gemma3:1b takes 22–23 iterations to clear the 8.0 threshold on plain technical nouns — leaving almost no headroom for harder terms. Still configurable in `config.yaml`. With gemma4:e2b (current default) most terms converge in 1–2 iterations, so the 50 cap is now safety budget, not the binding constraint. |
| ADR-018 | MPL labels are immutable once assigned. | Re-parenting changes tree edges and the denormalised `parent_label` field only; the label string itself never changes. Preserves the audit-log invariant that any historical reference to an MPL label resolves to the same entity. Cost: the visual reading of "MPL-X is at depth N because it has N segments" no longer matches reality once edges are re-attached — a child of MPL-002 can carry the label MPL-003 (assigned when it was top-level). Tree edges (`ontology_tree`) are authoritative for structure; numeric segments are only a creation-time hint. |
| ADR-019 | Human labels are approximate interfaces, not the ontology itself. | The MPL identifier (`MPL-NNN[.NNN…][a-z]?`) is the load-bearing address into machine-native semantic representations. `canonical_term`, `aliases`, and human-readable strings are operator-facing affordances that ease browsing and dictation, NOT the ontology's actual content. Implications: (a) the chat surface (`/api/chat`) treats natural language as input to a resolution step that returns MPL identifiers — the model is asked to cite MPL labels in its prose, not term names; (b) a single `canonical_term` can host multiple distinct meaning-vectors keyed by `context_id` (a `DefinitionContext` per ADR's polysemy stance) without ambiguity, because the underlying address is the (MPL, context_id) pair, not the human word; (c) glossary export shows MPL identifier as primary and the term as a secondary label, never the other way; (d) renaming a `canonical_term` is a cosmetic operation that does NOT change the entry's identity. This stance follows from the design principle "Mahalath clarifies what it means" — clarification operates on machine-native concept space, with human language as an approximate lens onto it. |
| ADR-010 | Confidence threshold 8.0 (out of 10) for accepting an outcome; below threshold goes to the undecided queue. | §3.2 default. Threshold is configurable. Confidence is on a 0.0–10.0 scale to match Tirzah's edge confidence scale. |
| ADR-011 | Watched `input/` folder for ingestion; archive to `processed/` after success. | §3.3 requirement. Matches Tirzah's watched-folder pattern; same APScheduler-style polling cadence is appropriate. |
| ADR-012 | Five runtime folders, all gitignored: `input/`, `processed/`, `ontology/`, `logs/`, `undecided/`. | §5 requirement. The folders themselves are committed (via `.gitkeep`) but their contents are not. |
| ADR-013 | Use `.restart.md` + `.session-log.md` handoff discipline. | Borrowed from Tirzah where it worked well for multi-agent coordination. `.restart.md` is canonical current state; `.session-log.md` is append-only chronological narrative. |
| ADR-014 | Mahalath remains runtime-independent of Tirzah. | The two systems share operating philosophy but serve different purposes. Coupling them at runtime would force one's evolution to drag the other. Code-reading cross-pollination is encouraged; imports across project boundaries are not. [Scoped 2026-06-13 by ADR-031: a single OPT-IN, operator-configured exception — synchronous Tirzah context-collation at ingestion — is permitted; the default and the no-integration mode keep strict independence, so Mahalath still runs standalone.] |
| ADR-015 | Source material is preserved verbatim. | Mahalath analyses source documents to extract candidate terms; it does not rewrite, summarise, or compress source. Matches Tirzah's source-preservation discipline and §3.3 of the requirements. |
| ADR-016 | Reject duplicate source files by SHA-256 checksum at ingest time. | Same content-based duplicate rejection Tirzah uses (its ADR-016). Avoids re-processing the same source under a different filename. |
| ADR-017 | Logical separation between Mahalath and Tirzah MongoDB databases. | Default database name `mahalath_dev` (configurable). Same Mongo instance; different database. Avoids any collection-name collision and lets each project evolve schemas independently. |
| ADR-020 | The retrieval layer reuses the existing schema; no parallel "retrieval node" document. | An external proposal suggested a second node shape (`codified_label`, `parent_id`, `path`, `meanings`, `variants`, opaque `mah_term_*` ids). That duplicates `ontology_entries` + `definitions` + `ontology_tree` + `definition_contexts`, which already carry every field it names. A second schema means a breaking migration and two sources of truth. Decision: retrieval is a *read view* over the current collections. The only additive schema changes permitted for retrieval are (a) a denormalised `path` (ancestor MPL labels) on `ontology_entries`, maintained on insert/reparent, and (b) an optional per-definition consensus score on `DefinitionVersion`. See `docs/retrieval-spec.md`. |
| ADR-021 | Codified labels stay opaque; retrieval never bakes semantics into the key. | The proposal's `MAH_BANK_FIN_20250610_V3` encodes domain + date + version *in the identifier*. That contradicts ADR-019 (labels are approximate interfaces, not the ontology) and ADR-018 (labels are immutable): a label that names its domain/version becomes wrong the moment a term is re-framed or re-versioned. Decision: the codified reference an LLM retrieves and cites is the MPL label (optionally the `(MPL, context_id)` pair for a specific frame). Domain lives in the tree `path` and `references_labels`; version lives in `definitions[].` order/timestamps; frame lives in `context_id`. Retrieval surfaces these as *fields* alongside the opaque label, never inside it. |
| ADR-022 | Retrieval surfaces all frames; the consuming LLM disambiguates. | For a matched human term, retrieval returns every codified meaning (one per `context_id` frame) with provenance — it does not pre-select "the" meaning, because only the caller holds the question/context that resolves the polysemy. The same API serves two consumer roles: a retrieval-LLM that pares the frame set and forwards survivors to an answer-LLM, or an answer-LLM that reasons over the full set directly. Each meaning is keyed by the `(mpl_label, context_id)` handle with `context_name` as its readable label; selection state lives with the caller, not in Mahalath (retrieval stays read-only). Resolves retrieval-spec Q1. |
| ADR-023 | Returned meanings are reference-closed. | A description written in codified terms is only interpretable if every codified term it cites is itself resolvable. So whenever an included meaning's description references other MPL labels (via `references_labels`), those entries are added to the bundle too — transitively until closed, with a visited-set cycle guard (same pattern as the staleness cascade). The closure is mandatory: token-budget pressure degrades the fidelity of deep closure nodes (compact label + active meaning instead of full provenance) but never drops a referenced term. v1 closes at entry-level reference granularity; per-frame reference tracking is a later refinement (retrieval-spec Q5). |
| ADR-024 | Intent annotates definitions; it never creates entries or enters labels. | Accepted 2026-06-11 (operator, resolving DQ-013). Inferred illocution (intent tags, intentionality, intent confidence) is stored as optional metadata on `DefinitionVersion`. It never justifies a new ontology entry, never partitions an existing entry, and never appears in an MPL label (ADR-021). Contradistinct splits remain driven by meaning difference alone (DQ-005). Prevents multiplicative ontology growth (frames × intents) and keeps the §4 neutrality NFR intact — intent is deployment metadata about the source, not semantics of the term. Full evaluation: `docs/intent-extension-evaluation.md`. |
| ADR-025 | Intent attribution uses ordinal intentionality and a separate intent confidence, both consensus-gated. | Accepted 2026-06-11 (operator, resolving DQ-013/DQ-014). `intentionality` is `low \| medium \| high` (never a float score); `intent_confidence` is on the standard 0–10 scale and is distinct from definitional confidence and from any future effectiveness measure (perlocution; out of scope). Model-sourced intent tags are stored only on multi-pass unanimity (S2.5 machinery); below-threshold attributions route to operator review. The I-D evaluation gate (unanimity rate on a real corpus run) is the go/no-go criterion for model-sourced attribution; operator-authored tags are safe regardless. Local models cannot support float-precision intent scores (S2.4 direction-variance evidence); a wrong-but-stored intent is worse than an absent one. |
| ADR-026 | Utterance-level semantic instances are out of Mahalath's scope. | Accepted 2026-06-11 (operator, resolving DQ-013). The intent-extension proposal's `semantic_instance` document (locution span + context + illocution per utterance) is passage/memory-shaped work and belongs to Tirzah if anywhere (ADR-014). Mahalath absorbs the concept-level residue only: per-definition intent annotation and (optionally) `source_quotes` locution anchoring on entries. |
| ADR-027 | Decision-effectiveness self-analysis is a read-only derived view; periodic snapshots are file-based, not a tenth collection. | Accepted 2026-06-12 (build-time, S2.39, closing requirements §3.4 "periodic self-analysis of decision-making effectiveness"). `analysis.py` computes the report by aggregating the existing audit collections (`decision_log`, `action_proposals` incl. operator verdicts, `undecided_queue`, `ontology_reviews`, `ontology_entries`) at read time — the analysis layer gets no Mongo write path, so analysing decisions can never mutate them. The headline metric is calibration: operator accept/reject verdicts bucketed by the agent confidence stated at proposal time. The "periodic" half (REM nightly tail + `effectiveness --snapshot`) appends one JSON line to `logs/effectiveness.jsonl`, following the per-document process-log precedent (ADR-012 folders): trend data accrues without a schema change, stays greppable, and is trivially erasable. Revisit a Mongo-backed snapshot store only if the operator wants in-DB trend queries. |
| ADR-028 | Multilingual support is discrete language lexicons as peers; no language is privileged and no canonical concept layer exists. | Accepted 2026-06-12 (operator, inline CLI discussion of the multilingual proposal). Each language's lexicon is built from its own evidence with its own tree; English is merely the first lexicon ingested. An MPL label addresses a meaning within one lexicon — the consuming citation is (language, label, frame), and the earlier "language-independent machine-native concept" framing is corrected accordingly. The proposal's Layer-2 "canonical semantic concepts" is NOT adopted: the stated purposes (translation creation/review via weighted mappings; cross-language illocution comparison) are fully served by pairwise mappings. A hub node may only ever be *promoted from* an accepted mapping clique if the data demands it — never created by ingestion or model initiative. Locale (country) is a plain attribute on definitions (evidence provenance, optional retrieval filter); it never creates structure — the proposal's variance-triggered branching clause is rejected. |
| ADR-029 | Cross-language mappings are first-class debated objects under the standard confidence constitution; alignment is never performed at ingestion. | Accepted 2026-06-12 (operator). A mapping is a semantic assertion between two lexicon entries: governed relationship taxonomy (equivalent / partial_overlap / narrower_than / …, a managed vocabulary like frames and intents), 0–10 confidence, N-pass attribution gated on the MAJORITY verdict — none included — with confidence = median across typed votes, promotion at the standard threshold, no-majority/under-threshold stored as unresolved (the undecided-queue pattern). [Amended 2026-06-12 (operator), relaxed from strict unanimity + min() after the first live de→en dry-run: families kept unanimously asserting relatedness while splitting partial_overlap vs narrower_than, and min() was hostage to one family's scale skew (the S2.42 pathology); a majority of none-votes now rejects, so a lone scout-model dissent cannot park junk pairs as unresolved. Minority votes are preserved verbatim in per_pass.] Mappings carry provenance + debate transcript + status lifecycle and participate in the staleness cascade (redefining either endpoint flags the mapping for re-audit). Generation happens in REM-style background consolidation, never during ingestion (deferred alignment prevents semantic contamination). Mapping output includes illocution-profile comparison of the endpoints — deployment divergence is translation-risk signal in its own right, computable because intent is attributed per-lexicon before any mapping exists. Empirical gate before model-sourced mappings are kept (the I-D pattern); embeddings-based candidate pruning (S-E) is a near-prerequisite at scale. |
| ADR-030 | One collection, global opaque label sequence, language as a field; retrieval never interleaves local and mapped results. | Accepted 2026-06-12 (operator). Entries gain an entry-level `language`; existing data backfills as "en". Labels stay one global opaque sequence (a label never reveals its language — ADR-021 extended). Single collection: compound (language, term) indexes match split-collection performance at vocabulary scale; Mongo's one-text-index limit plus per-document language stemming favours it; CJK needs the embeddings path. Splitting later is a filtered copy on the language key. Retrieval: query language is an explicit parameter (detection only as fallback); cross-language expansion is opt-in, depth-1 (no silent transitive composition); mapped results return in a separate labelled section carrying relationship/confidence/rationale — local and mapped scores are never blended (the ADR-022 "caller disambiguates" contract extended across languages). |
| ADR-031 | Tirzah context-collation is an optional, operator-configured, synchronous ingestion-time integration; opt-in only, scoping ADR-014. | Accepted (design) 2026-06-13 (operator); implementation deferred to v2. PURPOSE: raise the QUALITY of the context a debate sees by collating a candidate term's whole-document context before it is defined — calibrate the input so the lossy quantized-model "compression" yields a better definition. This is a DISTINCT capability from the local meaning-embedding/"fingerprint" work (which serves cross-language candidate shortlisting in M-C): embeddings find similar pieces; Tirzah collates them into a higher-fidelity, document-specific context. SHAPE: a synchronous request from Mahalath to Tirzah during ingestion (operator chose a live request over an offline hand-off), selected by a Mahalath config setting with three modes trading performance against quality — (a) `none`: no Tirzah, current local-section behaviour, fastest, preserves strict ADR-014 independence; (b) `fast`: a plain request for mechanical similarity retrieval, no model in Tirzah's loop; (c) `llm_brokered`: Tirzah uses a model to synthesise/compile the chunks, best quality, slowest. Modes (b)/(c) are the scoped runtime dependency on Tirzah that ADR-014 otherwise forbids; (a) and "feature off" keep Mahalath standalone. CONSTRAINTS for the build: define ingestion's fallback when Tirzah is unavailable or times out (degrade to `none`, retry, or fail the document — undecided); mode (c) stacks another local-LLM call into the ingestion path and is slow on current hardware (the ≥600s Ollama-timeout reality); the integration fixes definition ACCURACY (faithfulness to the document), not FLUENCY (grammar slips need the debate self-check, a separate lever). OPEN: the request contract depends on what Tirzah exposes (a queryable store vs a "document + term → collated context" call) — to be settled before implementation. |
| ADR-032 | Optional `hoglah` adapter: route generation AND embeddings through a Hoglah queue daemon instead of calling Ollama directly. | Accepted + implemented 2026-06-13 (operator). PURPOSE: for a walk-away run, serialize every model call through one durable local queue (Hoglah, concurrency default 1) so a single constrained GPU is not thrashed, with persistence/timeout enforcement across restarts. TOPOLOGY: a SEPARATE `hoglah run` worker daemon executes jobs off a shared SQLite queue and writes results to an output folder; Mahalath is a PURE SUBMITTER (`hoglah` client constructed `start_worker=False` — Hoglah ADR-016 ensures it never recovers/clobbers the daemon's in-flight jobs). Selected per channel via `model_adapter` / `embedding_adapter` / `chat_adapter = "hoglah"`; settings under `runtime.hoglah`. Keeps the existing synchronous `generate()`/`embed()` Adapter contract — the adapter submits then blocks on the result — so NO pipeline rework and other adapters are untouched. FINGERPRINTING: embeddings route through Hoglah's embedding jobs (ADR-013 there); the adapter maps Hoglah's non-finite-vector failure back to `EmbeddingNaNError` so existing NaN-resilience still applies. DELIVERY (config `delivery`): "poll" the output folder, or "callback" — Mahalath runs a tiny stdlib HTTP receiver and passes its OWN URL (`callback_host`/`callback_port`, port 0 = ephemeral) to Hoglah per job (nothing Mahalath-specific is baked into Hoglah; ADR-015 there is generic), with the output folder as automatic fallback if a push is missed. `hoglah` is an optional dependency (`pip install 'mahalath[hoglah]'`); the other adapters need it not installed. DISTINCT from ADR-031 (Tirzah, context QUALITY): this is an execution-transport choice, not a context-collation capability. |
| ADR-033 | Three prose layers per sense (`text` / `detailed_text` / scholarly) plus same-document lesson memory from debate transcripts. | Accepted (design) 2026-08-10 (operator); implementation pending. Full design: `docs/scholarly-layer.md`. SUMMARY: (1) Codified `text` remains the only authority for meaning; `detailed_text` (1.4.0) is pedagogical expansion of the same sense; a future scholarly layer is a third subordinate rendering (analytic, corpus-situated, epistemically honest) — never a second frame. (2) Full LLM debate trails stay in `decision_log` + `agent_exchanges` (ground truth). (3) Distilled **lesson cards** capture what worked / failed / must not repeat, and are injected into later debates. # Mahalath guide

## Capabilities in detail

### Two prose layers per definition

Each definition carries two layers of prose for the **same sense**: a short, multi-agent-debated `text` (the precise sense used for identity, consensus, and reference extraction) and an optional longer `detailed_text` exposition generated after accept for glossary readers and richer retrieval. Detailed text is not a second meaning or frame — it elaborates the accepted short definition. Generate on write with `runtime.generate_detailed_definitions` (default on), or fill a live corpus with `mahalath backfill-detailed --apply`.

### Polysemy as a first-class citizen

Definitions are tagged with a **context frame** (a governed taxonomy of `DefinitionContext` rows, authored per corpus). One entry can legitimately carry, say, a legal definition *and* an engineering one — they are co-equal; nothing supersedes anything. The web UI, chat, glossary export, and retrieval layer all group and label definitions by frame.

**`consensus_score` is pathway-specific.** The multi-agent debate path records a per-definition consensus score (min confidence across PrecisionCritic / SynthesisExplorer). The REM redefine path leaves it `null` while the stored wording is that single-model verdict. When overnight grounding is on and the explorer's revision receives exact-wording critic ratification, the stored score is the minimum across the grounding round. Operator-authored definitions have no consensus score. Older definitions may lack the field entirely (schema evolution); treat absence/`null` as "not a debate consensus," not as zero.

### External semantic grounding

The source document stays the primary evidence for what a term means in that document. `semantic_grounding.mode` chooses whether anything outside the corpus may be consulted after the ordinary debate:

- `corpus_only` (default) supplies no retrieved evidence. Use it for a corpus that should be read as self-defining.
- `hybrid` runs the corpus debate first and looks outward only when that debate's minimum confidence is strictly below `external_lookup_threshold` (default 8.0).
- `external` always looks up after the corpus debate.

Passages can clarify, discriminate, corroborate, challenge, or enrich. A revised definition is stored only when SynthesisExplorer proposes it and PrecisionCritic ratifies that exact wording as faithful to the source, neither dismisses or challenges the passages, the wording is not copied from an external passage, and every grounding score is at least as high as the corpus debate's. A challenge keeps the corpus wording and cannot raise confidence. A failed lookup or model call leaves the corpus decision, with failed model responses retained in the audit trail. The passages are an audit of that decision (`semantic_grounding`, plus a snapshot on the definition), not a web glossary. Retrieval, the glossary, and the entry page show the relation and how many sources were considered. Configure sources under `semantic_grounding.providers`: a local JSON file (`static`), MediaWiki search snippets (`wikipedia`), or an operator endpoint (`http`).

Stale definitions rewritten by the overnight REM job, and by `redefine-stale`, stay inside the corpus unless `semantic_grounding.overnight` is turned on. It defaults to off. With it on, that rewrite is still taken from the ontology first, and external lookup then follows the same mode and threshold. A result that does not clear the redefine confidence floor is not stored. REM re-debate of items still below the debate threshold follows `mode` on its own; the overnight flag does not gate it.

### Self-healing

Each entry records which other MPL labels its definitions mention (explicit + semantic matching, maintained incrementally on insert). When an upstream entry changes — redefined, re-parented, rolled back — every dependent is flagged stale, cascading with a cycle guard. Nightly REM jobs re-audit stale entries against current upstream state and either clear the flag or re-debate the definition.

### Retrieval layer (for an orchestrating LLM)

A typed read view over the ontology (`retrieval.py`), available as a library, CLI, and HTTP API:

- `search_terms` — resolve human terms to ranked matches (shared scorer + `$text` fuzzy index, branch/frame/status/confidence filters).
- `get_codified` — expand `MPL-004` (or the frame-scoped handle `MPL-004#physics`) into all meanings, tree path, references both directions, provenance, stale state.
- `build_bundle` — a **token-budgeted, prompt-ready bundle**: primary entries with *all* their frames (retrieval never collapses polysemy — the caller disambiguates), a mandatory **reference closure** (every codified term cited inside a returned description is included transitively, cycle-safe), ranked alternatives, and a compact NL rendering. Budget pressure trims breadth and verbosity in recorded steps; it never drops a frame or a closure node.
- `subtree` — limited-depth descendant summaries via the materialised ancestor path (one indexed query).
- `propose_term` — the one write path: a term the ontology doesn't confidently cover is enqueued onto the existing undecided path, where the normal REM re-debate machinery picks it up.

The same renderer backs retrieval text and the chat context block, so every consumer sees one idiom: MPL label primary, frame-grouped, provenance attached.

### Chat

`/api/chat` (and the `/chat` page) answers natural-language questions grounded in the live ontology — context selection by the shared scorer, frame-grouped prompts, MPL citations parsed back out for deep-linking, and tool-call action proposals (e.g. "X should be a child of Y") routed through the operator queue.

### Intent annotation

Beyond *what a term means*: *why the corpus deploys it* (speech-act illocution — teach, persuade, reassure, warn, …). Governed by hard guardrails (ADR-024/025/026): intent annotates definitions as source-deployment metadata; it never creates entries, never partitions an entry, never enters a label; intentionality is ordinal (low/medium/high), never a pseudo-precise float. All model-sourced tags pass an **N-pass unanimity gate** — a tag is stored only if every independent attribution pass proposes it, the ordinal only if all passes agree, and below-threshold attributions are withheld for operator review. The gate was validated empirically before rollout (15/15 unanimous attributions on real corpora, with minority tags and disagreed ordinals visibly dropped). New entries are attributed automatically at the pipeline tail; `backfill-intents` sweeps legacy definitions; retrieval filters by intent (`--intent teach`) without letting intent alter ranking.

### Decision-effectiveness self-analysis

The system periodically audits its own decision-making (`analysis.py`, read-only over the audit trails). The headline is **calibration**: every operator accept/reject/rollback on an agent proposal is a labelled data point for the confidence the agent stated when proposing — if operator acceptance doesn't rise with agent confidence, the threshold knobs are tuning noise, and the report says so in plain language. Also covered: debate outcome/iteration stats, REM re-debate resolution arcs (undecided → later accepted), undecided-queue health (items stuck at max escalation), hierarchy-review yield, and frame/intent coverage. `iterations_used` is the count of numbered transcript rounds, so a grounding round adds one to the persisted value and effectiveness averages; the in-memory corpus count remains separate for retry-cap decisions. Surfaced as `mahalath effectiveness` (text or JSON), the `/effectiveness` web page, `GET /api/effectiveness`, and a nightly JSON-line snapshot appended to `logs/effectiveness.jsonl` by the REM job.

## Operator workflows

### Understanding how a term was produced

Every model call that contributes prose to a term — the debate behind the short
definition, and the expansion behind `detailed_text` — records the full
conversation (`decision_log` + `agent_exchanges`), linked from the definition
(ADR-034). Read it with `mahalath show-decision <MPL-label|decision-log-id>`, or
from the entry page in the web UI, which lists every conversation and links to a
view of each.

### Review only what is actually stuck

The operator is asked about a term only once the system has finished trying
(ADR-037): below `runtime.confidence_threshold` it re-debates overnight, and it
surfaces after two retries if it is still short. `conflict` and
`moderator_block` — where the agents disagree on whether a term holds one
meaning or two — surface immediately, because more recursion does not settle
them. `mahalath needs-review` and the `/undecided` page show that set, with
accept/reject writing to the audit chain.

### Comparing runs over related material

`mahalath link-documents <document-id>` asks the model whether an incoming
document is related to one already processed — a revision, translation, excerpt
or shared material — and records the link. This is **not** deduplication: the
document is processed in full and the original's terms are untouched.
`--correspond` then matches terms across the pair, and
`mahalath compare-documents <link-id>` reports what differs — shared terms,
terms unique to each side, and definitions that changed. That is how you answer
whether a different model or a changed process improved the output (ADR-036).
Opt in at ingest with `runtime.link_related_documents`.

### Cross-language mappings (multilingual lexicons)

Mappings relate a term in one language to a term in another by *meaning*.
Candidates are found with meaning-fingerprints (embeddings), so the
embedding model must be pulled (`bge-m3`) and reachable.

```bash
# Compute a fingerprint for every entry (dry-run first; --apply writes).
.venv/bin/mahalath backfill-embeddings --apply

# Generate mappings between two lexicons (dry-run by default).
.venv/bin/mahalath generate-mappings --source-language de --target-language en
.venv/bin/mahalath generate-mappings --source-language de --target-language en --apply
.venv/bin/mahalath list-mappings --status accepted
```

> **Running under WSL2?** Generation reaches Ollama via the CLI, but
> embeddings use Ollama's HTTP API, which from WSL means the Windows host,
> not `localhost`. Set `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0` on the Windows side, restart
> Ollama, and set `ollama_base_url: http://wsl-gateway:11434` in
> `config.yaml` — the `wsl-gateway` host auto-resolves to the Windows
> gateway and survives WSL restarts.

For continuous operation, run the scheduler:

```bash
.venv/bin/mahalath run             # blocks; polls input/ every 60s, REM nightly at 02:00
.venv/bin/mahalath run --once      # cron-friendly: fire both jobs once and exit
```

For browser-based review + the JSON API:

```bash
.venv/bin/mahalath serve           # http://127.0.0.1:8000
# POST /api/chat          {question, focus_label?}
# POST /api/retrieve      {terms|labels, filters?, token_budget?, format?}
# POST /api/propose_term  {term, context?, near?, dry_run?}
```

For frontier-LLM review of the pending_review queue (operator-style adjudication by Claude):

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-…
.venv/bin/mahalath frontier-review --max-items 25
```

## Style overlay

A per-corpus voice-notes file makes definitions track the source's framing instead of generic dictionary fare:

```yaml
# config.yaml
runtime:
  style_overlay_path: docs/style-overlay.example.md
```

Per-document overrides:

```bash
.venv/bin/mahalath ingest-one input/book.md --style-overlay docs/voice-for-book.md
```

The overlay is injected into every agent prompt (extraction, debate, hierarchy review, redefine). In A/B testing this was the single biggest definition-quality lever.

## Routing via Hoglah (queue daemon)

By default Mahalath calls Ollama over HTTP (`model_adapter: ollama_http`; no
`ollama` binary required on PATH). For a
walk-away run you can instead route **both generation and embeddings** through
[Hoglah](https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/hoglah), a local-first job queue, so
every model call is serialized through one durable queue (handy on a single
constrained GPU). Hoglah's own [known limits](https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/hoglah#know-before-you-rely-on-it) apply.

```bash
pip install 'mahalath[hoglah]'
```

Set the adapter(s) to `hoglah` in `config.yaml` and configure the
`runtime.hoglah` block (see `config.example.yaml`). Then run a **separate**
Hoglah worker daemon pointed at the same queue + output folder:

```bash
HOGLAH_OUTPUT_DIR=~/.hoglah/outbox hoglah run --real   # executes jobs vs Ollama
```

Mahalath becomes a pure submitter: it enqueues each call and gets the result
back either by polling the output folder (`delivery: poll`) or via an HTTP
callback to a tiny receiver it runs (`delivery: callback`, with poll as
fallback). Mahalath owns the callback URL and sends it to Hoglah per job —
nothing about Mahalath is baked into Hoglah, so the same mechanism works for
any caller. Embedding/fingerprinting routes through Hoglah's embedding jobs
(`bge-m3`).

**Messaging transports.** Instead of the shared SQLite store, Mahalath can submit
over a broker — set `runtime.hoglah.transport` to `kafka`, `rabbitmq`, or `redis`
(default `store`). It then publishes a job-request message and awaits the result
over the same broker via Hoglah's `MessagingSubmitter`; a matching
`hoglah {kafka,rabbitmq,redis}-bridge` worker must run on the configured
topics/queues/streams. Install the broker client with the matching extra:
`pip install 'mahalath[hoglah-kafka]'` (or `hoglah-rabbitmq` / `hoglah-redis`).
